outcomes: Applications register dependencies by Go type or explicit token
The container rejects missing dependencies, cycles, duplicate providers, and invalid lifetime edges
Singleton and scoped resources are created once per owning lifetime and cleaned up deterministically
Concurrent first resolution returns one shared singleton without deadlock
nonGoals: Providing a process-global mutable service locator
Choosing the request or job boundaries that create and finalize scopes

requirements.text: Container close runs child cleanup before parent cleanup and runs close hooks in reverse registration order only for instances that were built.
Singleton instances live in the provider-owning container, scoped instances live in the requesting child scope, and root resolution of a scoped provider fails.
Constructor-based and token-based registrations share the same validation, cycle detection, visibility, tagging, and concurrency-safe resolution rules.
ContainerContext.Start validates the graph and eagerly resolves non-lazy singletons; a failure cleans up constructed singletons and returns the context to idle for a retry.
